I'm late to the party, but this reminds me of a wonderful children's book called The Empty Pot. The story is thus: a Chinese child named Ping has an amazing ability to grow the most beautiful flowers. The Emperor also loved flowers, but had no children of his own and needed to choose a successor. Children from all over the kingdom came before the Emperor where he announced he would choose one of them to take his place. He gave each of them a seed to plant and tend for one year. When they returned at the end of the year, the Emperor would judge their efforts and choose his successor.

Ping thought it would be easy and that he would surely be chosen to become the new Emperor. He planted his seed and watered it faithfully. However, his seed did not grow. He transferred the seed to a bigger pot, continued to water and tend it dutifully, but it never sprouted. At the end of the year, as all the other children in the kingdom ran by him with their pots of beautiful and fragrant flowers, Ping shamefacedly carried his empty pot to be judged by the Emperor. The Emperor walked amongst the children with an angry scowl upon his face, until he saw poor Ping. He asked Ping why he had brought him an empty pot. Ping began to cry as he explained how he had tried his best to tend the seed and make it grow, but it did not. The Emperor smiled and announced he had found his successor. He said, "I do not know where the rest of you children got your seeds, for the seeds I gave you had been boiled and could not grow."

It's a wonderful lesson in honesty and a treasured book in our home. I highly recommend it!

Glad to help out! I've been lasering for 5 years now and it still frustrates me but I love it. With some dedication and perseverance you will make cool things. Sounds like you are off to a good start already.

PVC/vinyl should never be run in a laser cutter because it releases chlorine gas and hydrochloric acid which will attack the metal parts and is an extreme breathing hazard. Acrylic, birch plywood and soft woods like alder work best and don't release corrosive fumes. 40 watts can get through quarter inch acrylic and birch plywood in two or three passes. I recommend using compressed air assist at all times to avoid damaging your optics. Clean your lens and mirrors regularly with 91% isopropyl alcohol or eyeglass lens wipes. You will also want to learn how to align the beam so you have the best results and always position the focal point to the surface of the work or a few millimeters below to cut clean. Oh one more thing, never leave the laser operating unattended because fire is always a risk. It'll take a while to get everything going fully so take your time and be patient. It's a great hobby so it's totally worth it.
